candidates.attacker_control: A remote unauthenticated client that can reach an AMQP port supporting protocol versions 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 (the standard distribution's default AMQP port advertises all installed protocols, including 0-8..0-9-1) fully controls the length-prefixed fields of the connection.start-ok frame. Two decode routes reach the unchecked allocations before SASL authentication completes: (1) EncodingUtils.readBytes is called while parsing the start-ok frame's SASL `response` field (ConnectionStartOkBody.java line 142), so a 4-byte length larger than the frame/heap triggers the allocation during parse; (2) the start-ok `client-properties` field table is decoded lazily but is forced open by AMQPConnection_0_8Impl.receiveConnectionStartOk -> setClientProperties (lines 1106 and 560-580), which calls clientProperties.get(...) before processSaslResponse; the table scan in FieldTable.findValueForKey (lines 463-488) reaches AMQTypedValue.readFromBuffer (lines 214-231) -> AMQType.LONG_STRING.readValueFromBuffer (lines 63-67) -> EncodingUtils.readLongString when an entry uses a type marker such as 'S' (LONG_STRING) or the binary type mapped to readLongstr with an over-declared 4-byte length (a value name equal to the first queried client property, e.g. the qpid.close_when_no_route key, reaches readFromBuffer directly).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Frame-level protections exist but do not mitigate: AMQDecoder.decodable enforces the negotiated maximum frame size (AMQDecoder.java 143-167) and AMQPConnection_0_8Impl.receiveConnectionTuneOk validates the client's frameMax (1193-1224), but these bound only the outer frame size; a frame of a few dozen bytes can still declare a 2 GiB inner length. FieldTable construction validates only that the table length fits the frame (QpidByteBuffer.view, MultiQpidByteBuffer 953-957), and skipLongString throws on out-of-range positions (EncodingUtils 247-254), so an oversized value encountered while scanning for a different key aborts rather than allocates - the allocation is reached when the oversized value is the requested key or is the SASL response field, which is the path described. The guarded AMQShortString reader (86-97) shows bounds validation was the intended pattern, supporting that this is an oversight rather than a design decision. I confirmed the start-ok frame is dispatched before authentication (setClientProperties precedes processSaslResponse) and that no layer between the decoder and the thread pool catches Error. I did not verify any of this at runtime (execution is out of scope) and did not confirm the corresponding upstream fix/CVE.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote denial of service: an attacker can force large heap allocations per connection, causing OutOfMemoryError in the broker JVM; with the default exception handler this terminates the broker process (full service outage) and, per the default launch script's -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError, writes heap dumps that can also exhaust disk. Lower-volume attempts degrade service through GC thrashing; with a very large declared length the allocation itself fails immediately, so no actual memory needs to be consumed by the client.
candidates.prerequisites: Network access to an enabled AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 port. No credentials are required: the vulnerable decode happens while processing connection.start-ok, before the SASL exchange is evaluated, and the default installation accepts the frame sequence (protocol header, server connection.start, client connection.start-ok). Effect is greatest with the default broker JVM heap (512 MB per broker/bin/qpid-server* and doc/java-broker Appendix-Environment-Variables); any declared length above the available free heap (e.g. 0x7FFFFFFF, or values > 2^31-1 yielding NegativeArraySizeException) triggers an OutOfMemoryError/error. Highest impact if the operator has not set -Dqpid.broker.exceptionHandler.continue=true.
candidates.root_cause: In broker-core EncodingUtils, length-prefixed values are decoded by reading a 4-byte unsigned length and immediately allocating `new byte[(int) length]` without verifying that the declared length is actually available in the remaining buffer: readLongString (lines 230-244), readLongstr (lines 256-270) and readBytes (lines 316-330). A declared length up to 0x7FFFFFFF therefore forces an allocation of up to ~2 GiB (or a NegativeArraySizeException for lengths > 2^31-1) from a tiny frame, and the missing check is asymmetric with the guarded short-string reader AMQShortString.readAMQShortStringAsBytes (lines 86-97), which does enforce `length > buffer.remaining()`; QpidByteBuffer.view (MultiQpidByteBuffer lines 953-957) likewise validates only the outer table length, not inner value lengths.
candidates.title: Pre-auth AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 decoding allocates byte arrays from unvalidated 4-byte length fields (remote OOM / broker termination)
candidates.trace: 1) ConnectionStartOkBody.process (lines 136-152) parses connection.start-ok in order: readFieldTable (lazy FieldTable; outer length is bounds-checked by QpidByteBuffer.view), AMQShortString mechanism, EncodingUtils.readBytes for the SASL response, locale. 2) EncodingUtils.readBytes (316-330) does `long length = buffer.getUnsignedInt(); ... new byte[(int) length]; buffer.get(dataBytes);` with no `length <= buffer.remaining()` check, so the array is allocated before the (underflowing) copy; readLongString (230-244) and readLongstr (256-270) have the identical pattern. 3) Field-table variant: `clientProperties.get(...)` in setClientProperties (560-580) -> FieldTable.getProperty/findValueForKey (101-110, 463-488) -> AMQTypedValue.readFromBuffer (214-231) -> AMQType LONG_STRING.readValueFromBuffer (AMQType.java 63-67) -> EncodingUtils.readLongString -> allocation. This path runs from receiveConnectionStartOk (1070-1109) before `processSaslResponse` authenticates the response. 4) The resulting OutOfMemoryError is not caught: AMQPConnection_0_8Impl.onReceive catches only AMQFrameDecodingException|IOException (246-259, and AbstractAMQPConnection.received only StoreException, 566-589); NonBlockingConnection.doWork catches only IOException|ConnectionScopedRuntimeException (248-318); SelectorThread.ConnectionProcessor.run (544-578) has no catch, so the Error reaches the thread-pool worker's uncaught-exception path. 5) Main.setExceptionHandler (443-498) installs a default handler that calls Runtime.getRuntime().halt(1) (line 489) unless the system property qpid.broker.exceptionHandler.continue is set; broker docs also state an OutOfMemoryError forces broker shutdown. Even under 'continue', repeated triggers/GC thrashing and the default -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError heap dumps provide a sustained DoS.
candidates.unverified: Runtime exploitability and the exact JVM outcome were not tested; the OOM-to-halt effect depends on the default UncaughtExceptionHandler being in effect (i.e., qpid.broker.exceptionHandler.continue not set), and the impact is reduced by larger heaps, connection-rate limits, or a custom exception handler. The exact intended upstream patch/CVE for this snapshot could not be confirmed offline. Whether all deployment profiles enable AMQP 0-8..0-9-1 auto-detection on the exposed port depends on the configured `protocols` attribute (the default shipped configuration does).
candidates.weakness_type: Uncontrolled resource consumption / allocation from untrusted length (CWE-400, CWE-789); pre-authentication denial of service

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 2,493-file Apache Qpid Broker-J 8.0.0-SNAPSHOT tree (Maven multi-module; main sources only - no src/test files are present in the snapshot, and no binary files were needed). P1 relation index reports complete coverage: all 2,493 files indexed, 65,209 edges, 30,177 symbols, no missing files or hash mismatches; index edges were used only for navigation and every cited edge was re-verified in source. Surveyed: AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 decoder and encoders (AMQDecoder, ServerDecoder, ConnectionStart/Tune/Open bodies, FieldTable, AMQType/AMQTypedValue, EncodingUtils, AMQShortString), AMQP 0-10 transport decoder/assembler, AMQP 1.0 framing/type handling, message conversion and MIME converters (including JMS map/stream parsing), management HTTP authentication filters/servlets/controllers and converters, access-control rule sets and ACL file parsing, authentication managers (plain/MD5/OAuth2 identity resolvers), storage serdes (JDBC/Derby/BDB), and the broker main/exception-handling path. The submitted candidate was traced end-to-end in source from the network frame to the uncaught-exception handler.
limitations: Static review only: no build, test, scanner execution, or runtime confirmation was performed (and none is permitted in this run).
The snapshot contains no test sources, so regression tests that might confirm or bound the behavior were unavailable.

Only a survey-level review was possible for large secondary areas (BDB/JDBC store implementations, OAuth2 providers, management console JavaScript, websocket plugin), so those areas are not fully covered.
The P1 index is navigational (syntactic candidates, no control/data-flow or reachability proof); all statements about data flow in the finding come from manual source reading, not the index.
Mapping the finding to a specific upstream fix/CVE was not possible without external data, and external/advisory lookups were out of scope.
Impact details that depend on deployment configuration (JVM heap size, qpid.broker.exceptionHandler.continue, connection limits, enabled protocol set) could not be validated against a running system.

rejected_leads.lead: TypedBytesContentReader.readObject (broker-core typedmessage) allocates new byte[size] from an attacker-controlled JMS map/stream byte-array length, reachable via MessageConverter_v0_8_to_Internal/MessageConverter_v0_10_to_Internal and MessageConverter_to_1_0.getBodySection when a message with content type jms/map-message or jms/stream-message is viewed via the management API with returnJson=true or consumed by a cross-protocol consumer.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible same-class DoS, but requires an authenticated publisher plus a conversion trigger (management access or an AMQP 1.0 consumer), so it is not as strong as the pre-authentication allocation path for this snapshot; not submitted because of the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: GZIPUtils.uncompressStreamToArray/uncompressBufferToArray decompress message content without any size limit, and the same conversion paths (management returnJson preview, AMQP 1.0 delivery) inflate it into a ByteArrayOutputStream.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible gzip-bomb DoS in the same conversion channel, but it is a design-level resource limit issue in a utility used in several features and I could not confirm a remote, unauthenticated trigger; not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: InternalMessage / InternalMessageMetaDataType use java.io.ObjectInputStream to deserialize stored INTERNAL message metadata and bodies.
rejected_leads.reason: The INTERNAL metadata ordinal is chosen by the broker's own writers, not by wire input; I found no remote path that lets an attacker control stored bytes for that type, so the deserialization lead was not substantiated.

rejected_leads.lead: PluginClassProviderAction.perform loads classes by request parameter via Class.forName("org.apache.qpid.server.plugin." + className).
rejected_leads.reason: Class name is constrained to a fixed package and the result is only used with QpidServiceLoader; no dangerous sink or class-initializer abuse was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: FileServlet builds a classpath resource path from request.getServletPath()/getPathInfo() and opens it.
rejected_leads.reason: Potential traversal depends on container URI normalization (Jetty) and classpath layout; no source-level evidence of an accessible out-of-bounds resource, so it remains unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: AMQP frame-size handling in v0-8 (max frame size, tune-ok validation) and v0-10 (ServerInputHandler size checks) / v1.0 (FrameHandler size checks).
rejected_leads.reason: Reviewed as a possible DoS vector; these checks are present and bound frame sizes correctly, so no candidate there.

summary: Snapshot is Apache Qpid Broker-J 8.0.0-SNAPSHOT (multi-module Java broker; 2,493 main-source files, no tests present). I surveyed protocol decoders (AMQP 0-8/0-10/1.0), management HTTP auth/servlets, access-control rules, message conversion/MIME converters, store serdes and OAuth2 authenticators, then traced the strongest issue in source. Single candidate submitted: unauthenticated remote denial of service via unbounded array allocation in AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 decoding (broker-core EncodingUtils). The broker reads 4-byte length prefixes and calls `new byte[length]` before checking that the declared length fits in the received frame, on the pre-authentication `connection.start-ok` path; the resulting OutOfMemoryError is not caught by the I/O stack and reaches the default uncaught-exception handler that halts the JVM. Other plausible but weaker leads (JMS map/stream conversion allocation, gzip decompression, INTERNAL metadata deserialization) are listed as unconfirmed/rejected and are not submitted as additional candidates.
